# Questions for Javatri

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs`. Edit prisma/source-data.ts, not this file. -->

Nothing in this list has been guessed. Where the old site was ambiguous, contradictory or empty, the
new site carries the scraped value forward unchanged, flags it, and waits for you.

There are **6 blockers** (the site should not go live until these are answered),
**16 important** items and **1** tidy-ups.

Most of the answers can be entered by your staff at `/admin` without a developer. Where that is
true, the answer says so.

---

## Blockers

These either cost you money every day they are wrong, or carry legal risk.

### 1. We need the 14 FSA allergens for every dish before launch.

There is no allergen information anywhere on the current site. Under assimilated Regulation (EU) 1169/2011 this information has to be available for every dish sold, and for distance selling it has to be available both before the order is placed and again when it is delivered.

**What we did in the meantime.** Built the whole allergen system — a field on every dish, a filter on the menu, a display on every dish card, and the standard notice on the menu and at checkout — and left the data empty, because guessing an allergen is dangerous. Until an item is confirmed the site says "allergen information not yet confirmed, please call us", which is honest rather than reassuring. ALLERGEN_TODO.md is the list to work through; it can be filled in at /admin/menu.

### 2. What are your delivery radius, minimum order, delivery fee and free-delivery threshold?

The old site has no delivery of its own — delivery goes through Just Eat — so there was nothing to carry over. These four numbers decide whether a delivery order is profitable, so we are not guessing them for you.

**What we did in the meantime.** Seeded placeholders: 4 mile radius, £20.00 minimum, £3.49 fee, free over £45.00. All four are editable at /admin/branch. If you would rather not do your own delivery at all, switch delivery off there and the site offers collection and dine-in only.

### 3. Which set of opening hours is correct?

Three different sets are published right now:
  • Homepage block: Mon–Thu 15:00-22:00, Fri 12:00-22:00, Sat 12:00-22:00, Sun 12:00-20:00
  • Menu header text: MON-THURSDAY 15:00-22:00, FRIDAY-SUNDAY 12:00-22:00
  • Google Business Profile: Mon 12:00–20:00, Tue–Fri 15:00–22:00, Sat 12:00–22:00, Sun 12:00–22:00
The homepage and Google disagree about Monday and Sunday. The menu header and the homepage
disagree about Sunday closing (22:00 vs 20:00).
This is a blocker because the ordering system refuses orders outside opening hours — wrong
hours means turning away money, or taking orders the kitchen is not there to cook.

**What we did in the meantime.** Seeded the homepage block. Staff can correct it at /admin/hours in under a minute — no developer needed. Please also update the Google Business Profile to match, since that is what most people actually see.

### 4. Please re-supply the Drinks Delight (Bar).

BROKEN ON LIVE SITE - page renders empty. Partial data recovered from Google's cached index only. Full bar list must be re-supplied by the restaurant.
Google still has this menu indexed with prices, so people search for it, click through and land on a blank page.

**What we did in the meantime.** Seeded unpublished so nothing half-recovered goes on sale, and 301-redirected the old indexed URL to /menu so those visitors land on a working menu instead of an empty page. Send the list and it can be published from /admin.

### 5. Please re-supply the Pub Menu.

BROKEN ON LIVE SITE - page renders empty but is still indexed by Google. Only fragments recovered (e.g. a pasta dish at 6.45, 'Steak and chips' - sirloin marinated with rosemary and garlic, served with egg and chips). Full menu must be re-supplied or the page retired with a 301.
Google still has this menu indexed with prices, so people search for it, click through and land on a blank page.

**What we did in the meantime.** Seeded unpublished so nothing half-recovered goes on sale, and 301-redirected the old indexed URL to /menu so those visitors land on a working menu instead of an empty page. Send the list and it can be published from /admin.

### 6. What is the correct price for aloo parantha?

  • £6.50 on the Food Menu
  • £8.50 on the Indian Street Food

**What we did in the meantime.** Both prices were seeded as scraped, on their respective menus, so nothing was silently changed. This is exactly the failure the old two-copies-of-the-menu setup produced; on the new site there is one row per dish, so once you tell us the price it can only be right or wrong in one place.

## Important

Worth answering before launch, but not fatal.

### 1. Is Javatri Farnham Common open, and what are its address, phone and hours?

The old site advertises it on the homepage and offers it in the banqueting enquiry form, but publishes no address, no phone number and no opening hours, and it cannot be selected for ordering or booking. A customer who picks it in the form has no way to find it.

**What we did in the meantime.** Seeded as an inactive branch. It does not appear as an option anywhere on the new site. Send us the details and it can be switched on in /admin without a rebuild — the schema already supports multiple branches.

### 2. Is "Vegetable Momos" vegetarian?

It sits in "Classic Indian Street Bite (Veg)", which reads as a vegetarian section, but the live site carries no vegetarian tag on the dish itself. The two contradict each other.

**What we did in the meantime.** Seeded exactly what the site says — no vegetarian tag — because labelling a dish vegetarian when it is not is as serious as getting an allergen wrong. It will not appear under the "Vegetarian" filter until you confirm it.

### 14. Do you want to keep the Just Eat listing now that ordering works directly?

You currently also sell through https://www.just-eat.co.uk/restaurants-javatri-at-the-bell-and-bottle-maidenhead/menu. Every order placed there costs you commission; the same order placed on this site costs you Stripe's fee and nothing else.

**What we did in the meantime.** Not linked from the new site. Direct ordering is the primary call to action everywhere. Tell us if you want the Just Eat link back as a secondary option.

### 15. Would you like descriptions written for the Indian Street Food dishes?

The live site publishes these dishes as bare names and prices, with no descriptions at all, while every dish on the main food menu has one. A dosa with a sentence under it sells better than a dosa without.

**What we did in the meantime.** Seeded them with no description rather than writing copy and putting words in your mouth. They render cleanly without one, and descriptions can be added at /admin/menu at any time.

### 16. Can we have some photographs?

There is almost no usable photography of the restaurant, the food or the banqueting hall. The new site is designed to work without it — the homepage earns its impact typographically rather than with a stock curry photograph, which would have been a lie about your food — but photographs of your actual dishes sell them better than any amount of design does, and the events page in particular is asking people to book a room they cannot see.

**What we did in the meantime.** Every dish now carries a stand-in photograph — a library picture of that *kind* of dish, taken from Wikimedia Commons under a licence that permits commercial use, with the photographer named on /photo-credits. The menu says plainly that these are serving suggestions rather than our plates, because a photograph next to a price makes a promise and these cannot keep it.

They are a stopgap, and not a good one: they are other people's kitchens, shot on other people's phones. Send us a phone-camera set of the hall dressed for a wedding and a dozen of your best-selling dishes and each real photograph replaces its stand-in the moment it goes on the dish — no code change, the real one always wins. The events page still has no photography at all.
